evidence.source: Wikisource, received Shuowen Jiezi 欠部
evidence.field: 欠部 entries 欠 and 歌
evidence.text: The received text defines 欠 as an open mouth with breath rising out and defines 歌 as ‘to chant/sing,’ analyzing it as 从欠哥聲. This supports the Shuowen analysis of 欠 as semantic classifier and 哥 as phonetic component in that form; it does not establish the earliest form of 歌.
evidence.title: 說文解字/08 - 維基文庫

evidence.text: The compilation labels a reported form on the late Spring-and-Autumn 余贎兒鐘 (集成184), and also lists Warring States, Chu manuscript, received Shuowen, and Qin Shuihudi forms. It describes an early form as 言+可 and later forms as 欠+哥, but this is secondary analysis; the examples do not establish a continuous lineage or rule out related spellings or variants. Its claim that 哥 contributes meaning is not supported by the Shuowen phonetic notation.
evidence.title: 歌字形演变字源_汉字「歌」

evidence.text: The page gives Mandarin gē (Pinyin), Middle Chinese ka in its listed romanization, Baxter–Sagart (2014) Old Chinese *[k]ˤaj, and Zhengzhang (2003) Old Chinese *kaːl for 歌. Its Zhengzhang entry identifies 可 as phonetic. These are reconstructions rather than direct recordings; compare only forms within the same reconstruction system.
evidence.title: 歌 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry cites 《詩經·魏風·園有桃》 for the verbal use of 歌 in ‘心之憂矣，我歌且謠’ and records later senses including praise and song or poetic forms. The cited poem is not dated on this page, so it does not establish a date for the composition, the surviving witness, or the earliest physical graph. Dictionary sense order is not semantic chronology.

evidence.source: Wikimedia Commons file description page, found in web search results; direct page open failed
evidence.text: The search result describes 歌-seal.svg as a vector depicting 歌 in Shuowen seal-script style and reports CC0 for structured file data. Opening the Commons description page failed with a cache miss in this web interface, so the description and reuse status could not be rechecked on the opened page during this stage. This is a modern vector redraw, not an ancient artifact photograph.
evidence.title: File:歌-seal.svg - Wikimedia Commons

search_audit.outcome: Search found the Commons file description and stated the image depicts 歌 in Shuowen seal-script style, with a CC0 notice for structured file data. Opening the description page failed with a cache miss.

search_audit.query: 歌 seal script character Commons image 歌
search_audit.outcome: Search surfaced the same Commons file as a candidate; no additional verified image candidates found.

search_audit.query: Opened received Shuowen 欠部 text, Taiwan MOE dictionary entry, Wiktionary 歌 entry, 39017 form collation
search_audit.outcome: Inspected the opened pages. Shuowen supports the 欠 semantic and 哥 phonetic analysis of its received form; 39017 reports earlier forms but does not establish their lineage. The MOE dictionary cites Shijing use without dating the composition. Wiktionary provides readings and reconstruction values for 歌.

search_audit.query: Opened Commons Special:Redirect/file and MediaWiki API imageinfo for 歌-seal.svg
search_audit.outcome: Both direct endpoint requests were inaccessible through the web tool. No direct image URL could be verified from the source page.

gaps: The Commons file description search result names 歌-seal.svg but the description page and direct file endpoints could not be opened in this invocation. The prior packet's acquisition finding reports a 404 for its candidate direct image URL. Since an actual working direct image URL could not be verified, no glyph image is selected.

The early 言+可 and received 欠+哥 forms are reported in a secondary collation. Their chronological relationship, component ancestry, and whether they are variants or related spellings remain unresolved; the artifact/facsimile pixels were not independently checked.

The Shijing citation supports an early textual use claim in reference works, but no date of composition or surviving written witness was established here. Earliest secure physical attestation remains unresolved.
The consulted sources do not establish a chronology or pathway among singing, song, praise, and poetic-genre senses. No whole-graph borrowing account is established.

limitations.text: No image selected: Commons search identified a modern Shuowen seal-style redraw, but opening its file page failed and the direct image endpoints were inaccessible. The exact candidate direct URL in the prior acquisition finding was reported as 404, so identity and reuse provenance could not be adequately reverified for an image selection.
